blocking.section: Binary upgrades > In-place handover (step 6); Binary upgrades > Drain timeline defaults
blocking.issue: New regression from the readiness fix. The Drain definition this document owns, which its Guarantees table quotes verbatim from pack section 11, says a Drain starts with readiness failing. The same pack row says the old process Drains in a Zero-Downtime Upgrade. Pack 8.5 also allows `/readyz` 200 only when the Node is not draining. The revised text instead defines a handover Drain with no readiness failure, and has the old process answer in-flight `/readyz` requests with 200. The fix can keep ZG-3: step 6 already moves every probe connection to the new process before the Drain starts at step 7, so the Drain can fail readiness with no balancer seeing it.
blocking.evidence: Line 46: "| Drain | Graceful shutdown of a Node: readiness fails, listeners stop accepting, HTTP/2 GOAWAY is sent, ..."; line 47: "then the old process Drains"; line 184: "answering in-flight admin requests with `Connection: close` moves keep-alive health checkers to the new process; the old one never serves a 503 `/readyz`"; line 208: "A handover skips the 503 (step 6) and the accept window". Pack 8.5: "`ruralzd` `/readyz` | 200 only when an active validated Revision is loaded, every `secretRef` it uses has resolved, listeners are bound and the Node is not draining".
blocking.fix: Line 208: "In a handover the old process fails `/readyz` at Drain start like any Drain, but step 6 has already moved every probe connection to the new process, so no balancer sees the 503; it skips the accept window, so its Drain deadline falls 20 s after steering (target)." Step 6: "...moves keep-alive health checkers to the new process before the Drain starts, so no balancer sees the old process's 503." If the old process must still answer 200 after Drain start, add an Open question proposing a pack 8.5 and section 11 clarification instead.

blocking.section: Verification runbook (Before rows); Control plane upgrades (Prepare)
blocking.issue: The revised Before rows gate the skew check on Node binary versions. The command they name cannot show versions. The CLI reference says `ruralz node list` shows only active and Last-Known-Good digests. Release, versioning and compatibility says Ruralz Control cannot learn a Node's binary version after an upgrade or rollback until OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-4 closes (blocking for Planned (M2) skew checks). As written, operators cannot run the gate that acceptance criterion 3 depends on.
blocking.evidence: Line 430: "| Before a Ruralz Control upgrade | `ruralz version`; `ruralz node list --cluster <name>`; ... | Every Node at N-1; ..."; line 431: "| Before a Node upgrade, after finalize | `ruralz node list --cluster <name>` | Every Node at N-1 or N; ...". CLI and API surface: "| `ruralz node list` | Nodes with active and Last-Known-Good digests | `--cluster NAME` |". Release: "Only `EnrollRequest` carries a binary `version` (`Hello` carries the anchor set's), which goes stale after an upgrade or rollback (OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-4 ...)".
blocking.fix: In both Before rows, keep `ruralz node list` for the digest checks. For versions, read each Node's `service.version` telemetry resource attribute ([Observability](../architecture/10-observability.md)) or the host or image inventory. Add "until OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-4 lets `ruralz node list` show binary versions". Tag `ruralz version` as checking only the CLI's own version (it must be N or N-1).

blocking.issue: The revised Atomic swap paragraph says the latest pending Revision waits up to 37 s for the closing snapshot. This contradicts the System overview, a foundation document, which says activation never waits. Data plane records the conflict as OQ-data-plane-13, owned by system-overview and still open. This document cites Data plane's rule 6 but not the Open question, so it states undecided behavior as settled.
blocking.evidence: Line 92: "The latest pending Revision waits for that snapshot's release (rule 6 there), up to 37 s plus the largest Plugin `limits.timeout` (target), within the 60 s ACK timeout (target) while that timeout is under 23 s." System overview, Compile before swap: "At most K = 2 retired snapshots are kept (target); activation never waits, so at the limit streams pinned to the oldest get an immediate graceful close". Data plane: "| OQ-data-plane-13 | Should System overview's \"activation never waits\" be amended so a grace period is never cut short? | (a) The latest pending Revision waits ... (current); (b) never wait ... | system-overview | No |".
blocking.fix: Append to that sentence: "pending OQ-data-plane-13, which would amend System overview's 'activation never waits'; under its option (b) the closing snapshot's pins end at once and no wait applies".

non_blocking.section: Rollback (Ruralz Control after finalize, Nodes at N)
non_blocking.suggestion: Step 1 points to two steps of another row, and step 3 bundles the restore, the CRD re-apply and the relay redeploy. Say that each step is one operation per Cluster and that High availability and disaster recovery owns the restore's internal steps. That keeps the ZG-8 claim of three steps or fewer defensible.

"`ruralz_control_cluster_nodes` drops at most 10% (target)" applies to every upgrade. Line 339 admits that each replica replacement unqualifies its Nodes until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 closes. Qualify the row as V-5 does: "after OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a); until then, only Clusters with declared ceilings".

Line 70 says "parse and schema checks (RZ-CFG-001 to RZ-CFG-013)", but that range also covers reference and substitution codes (RZ-CFG-008 to RZ-CFG-013), and schema-stage codes such as RZ-CFG-016 and RZ-CFG-030 fall outside it. Write "the Configuration model's file-mode stages up to reference resolution".
Links to ADR-0015 and ADR-0016 still produce WARN lines because those files do not exist yet. Recheck them once the ADRs land.
